question.problem: What is ${\int }_{-4}^{-1}\sqrt{5}{x}^{-4}\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-1}\sqrt{5}{x}^{-4}\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\sqrt{5}{x}^{-4},$ the lower bound is $a=-4$ and the upper bound is $b=-1.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{-1-(-4)}{n}=\frac{3}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-1}\sqrt{5}{x}^{-4}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(-4+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(-4+\frac{3i}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[\sqrt{5}{(-4+\frac{3i}{n})}^{-4}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
